subject: Post-demo: SLO & token limits impact on latency (next steps)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@haven-robotics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: SLO & token limits impact on latency (next steps)

Sam — great to meet today, thanks for the detailed walkthrough of the captioning pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment on SLOs and what to validate in the POC:

Summary of constraints you shared:
- Target tail latency: P95 <= 300 ms for live captions (streaming, per-chunk).
- Avg request size: 400–800 input tokens (speech-to-text output chunk plus context).
- Response size: 100–600 output tokens depending on rephrasing & punctuation.
- Expected concurrency during peak: 80–120 concurrent streams (each stream sends chunks ~1.5s).
- Hard requirement: independent stream isolation (no cross-stream cache leaks) and ability to degrade gracefully to lower-cost model on overload.

Initial qualification notes (from our runtime team):
- With a 1,024 token KV cache window and continuous streaming, we expect a per-token incremental latency of ~8–12 ms on A100-class instances when batch sizes are small; end-to-end P95 will depend heavily on batching and network hop.
- Large input windows (>=2,048 tokens) begin to push decoder pass times non-linearly — worst-case single-request decode can add 200–400 ms unless we use quantized kernels and smaller beam sizes.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Technical workshop (90m) with your infra + our runtime: validate concurrency pattern, chunk cadence, and confirm exact tokenization behavior (we'll provide a tokenization sample).
2) Deliver a small perf-runbook with scenarios (we'll include an estimated cost model for Dedicated vs Hosted for your concurrency). [Attachment: perf-runbook.xlsx]
3) Priyom will propose a two-phase POC:
   - Phase A: controlled canary (50 concurrent simulated streams, fixed 512 token windows) to measure baseline P50/P95, KV cache hit-rate, and batching effects.
   - Phase B: scale to 120 concurrent streams with realistic irregular chunk timing and test graceful degradation paths.

Can you confirm availability for the workshop next week (options: Tue 02/16 16:00 ET or Thu 02/18 11:00 ET)? Also please give us one sample transcript chunk (redacted) so we can pre-compute token counts.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com
[Attachment: perf-runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)]

From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@haven-robotics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 21:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO & token limits impact on latency (next steps)

Alex — thanks for the clean recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
- The 300 ms P95 is measured from when a chunk arrives at the ingress to when the caption text is emitted (end-to-end for that chunk). Network hops inside our region add ~30–50 ms we can't remove.
- Typical chunk is 1.5s audio -> roughly 200–350 tokens after ASR (varies by language and verbosity).
- For redundancy we want to keep two quality tiers: "high-fidelity" (context up to 2,048 tokens) and "fast" (limit input context to 512 tokens, cheaper model).

Workshop: Thu 02/18 11:00 ET works best for our infra lead. I'll drop a sample redacted transcript and our traffic trace for a 2-hour peak window.

Sam Wu
Head of Product Engineering | Haven Robotics
sam.wu@haven-robotics.com
[Attachment: peak-traffic-trace.json (log stub)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Sam Wu <sam.wu@haven-robotics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 00:10:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Post-demo: SLO & token limits impact on latency (next steps)

Sam / Alex — digging into what the runtime team will validate in the POC. High-level technical plan and hypotheses below. I'm calling out where we need exact inputs from Haven to make estimates realistic.

What we'll measure in Phase A (controlled canary):
- P50/P95/P99 decode time per chunk by token-window (256 / 512 / 1024 / 2048).
- KV cache hit rate impact when streams maintain a persistent session ID.
- Effect of batching with arrival jitter: target micro-batch sizes {1,2,4,8} and corresponding latency impact.

Key assumptions and sensitivity:
- Model family: we'll test a 16B/8-bit quantized variant and a 7B float16 variant. 16B quantized expected token time ~10–14ms (small batches), 7B ff16 ~5–8ms.
- Network serialization & TLS overhead: ~10–20 ms one-way in our hosted environment; if you run Dedicated inside your VPC we can shave this but need network layout.
- Chunk processing pipeline: ASR -> tokenization -> model decode -> post-processing. ASR time is external to Redwood; our focus starts at tokenization ingress.

Requests for accurate test configs (we need these before the workshop):
1) Representative tokenized chunk histogram (bins: 0-200, 200-400, 400-800, >800).
2) Realistic concurrency ramp pattern (how quickly do you expect spikes?).
3) Requirements for session affinity and KV cache scoping (per-user, per-device, per-conference).

POC telemetry we'll deliver:
- Per-request latency traces (breakdown: ingress parse, KV lookup, decode, post-process).
- Token-level throughput and GPU utilization heatmaps.
- Cost estimate per-hour and per-1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated run profiles.

Hedges / fallback plan:
- If P95 exceeds 300 ms at target concurrency on the high-fidelity model, automatic fallback policy: route to 7B fast model for new chunks while allowing in-progress long-decode chunks to finish.
- We can enable prefix-KV caching to reduce decode work for repeated context, but that requires stable session IDs from your side.

I'll prepare a short SLO handoff doc (redwood-slo-handoff.md) with all test matrices and attach it to the workshop invite.

Priyom Das
Principal Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-slo-handoff.md (text stub), perf-sim-results.csv (csv stub)]
